title: Dating With Herpes: Rebuilding Confidence and Mental Health After HSV-1 Diagnosis
summary: Diagnosed with HSV-1, I thought my dating life was over. Here is what dating with herpes taught me about disclosure, safety, and self-worth.
body_markdown:
## Dating With Herpes and Your Mental Health


Although it usually shocks most people when I say this, I think that living with herpes has actually improved my dating life in some ways. This is primarily true because of the level of confidence and self-assuredness it has forced me to develop. Disclosing a herpes diagnosis requires a level of calm, confidence in knowledge, and emotional resilience that is pretty unique to this experience. Not only do you need to be prepared to answer basic questions about the condition that a potential partner may have, but you should also be prepared for rejection.


Even though it is tough to accept, you have to be OK with the possibility that your potential partner will view your HSV as a dealbreaker. Some people just cannot see past the stigma, and even though that is a shame, you cannot take it personally and let it impact your[self worth](https://lifestance.com/condition/low-self-esteem/) . You have to understand that it does not say anything about who you are as a person, and work to move on emotionally.


I have been very lucky in my experience dating with herpes. I have disclosed my condition to a few dozen people, at least, and only once have I ever faced rejection for it. Even in that situation, the potential partner I had met was very kind, gentle, and apologetic about it. Was I upset? Of course. I really liked that person and we had an incredibly strong connection. But ultimately, I understood that it was their choice, and I did not feel it necessary or worth the time and effort to try and convince them to change their mind. I was sad for a little while, but I was very intentional in making sure that I did not take that sadness on as guilt or shame. Their choice had nothing to do with me personally.
